messages:
nisha: saw a 300-800ms tail latency spike on the KV-heavy long-context workload around 11:13. Rolling back to yesterday's commit removes it :thinking:
kevin: spike correlates with >2M token sessions? any eviction logs around that time?
alex: pushed a tiny flamegraph and trace from the host where it occurred — attaching short excerpt:
```
KV::evict_batch  45%  (alloc scan + unlink)
page_fault_handler  20%  (cold page reads)
runtime::kernel_select  12% (select path fallback)
rpc_send  8%
```
maria: interesting — flame shows a lot of time in evict + page fault handler. Could be repeated evictions touching memory that then faults back in. Did we change eviction policy config?
nisha: we flipped a FIFO tweak last week for better throughput on short chats. config shows fifo_window=128, eviction_batch=32.
kevin: fifo can be correct, but I remember a reinsertion pattern in our LRU->FIFO shim where items evicted from the main list get requeued when partial reuse happens. If that happens under pressure it can cause a churn loop.
alex: i grep'd the logs, here's a condensed pattern from the host (only relevant lines):
```
[11:12:51] evict: evicted shard=7 key=k23
[11:12:51] reuse: reinsert shard=7 key=k23 (partial hit)
[11:12:51] evict: evicted shard=7 key=k45
[11:12:51] evict: evicted shard=7 key=k23
[11:12:51] reuse: reinsert shard=7 key=k23
```
kevin: that exactly looks like reinsertion thrash. FIFO reinserts to tail, but if reuse occurs right after eviction we end up moving the key again, causing fragmentation and extra page touches.
maria: fragmentation = many small KV pages with low occupancy -> more page faults, more scanning during eviction. Also our kernel selector was falling back to a conservative path for long sequences which increases memory working set per request. Two orthogonal changes combined badly.
sam: can we repro locally with a synthetic generator? I can craft a workload that repeatedly partially re-requests recently-evicted keys and drive memory pressure.
nisha: yes please. repro steps: 1) set fifo_window=128 eviction_batch=32, 2) create sessions with context length 1.8M tokens that reference repeating token spans (simulate reuse), 3) run with small mem cap (emulate 16GB).
perf-bot: perf-summary (11:12 window): P50=18ms P95=120ms P99=340ms. Eviction throughput dropped by 40% vs baseline. Page fault rate +3.2x.
nisha: patch idea: 2-pronged: short-term throttle long-context requests when eviction pressure > threshold; medium-term: change reinsertion to a deferred requeue where we batch reinserts and dedupe within an epoch; long-term: move FIFO shim to a policy that avoids immediate requeue on partial-hit (treat partial-hit as a read-only hot mark instead of full reinsert).
kevin: prefer deferred requeue + make reinsertion idempotent. Implementation sketch:
```
on_partial_hit(key):
  hot_epoch = current_epoch()
  hot_set.insert_if_absent(key, hot_epoch)
end
evict_loop():
  process_hot_set_epoched()
  evict_batch()
end
```
maria: also tune kernel_select heuristics to prefer the compact path for these long contexts, that will reduce working set.
alex: i can prototype the deferred requeue and a small metric for "reinsert_rate" so we can alert if it climbs.
sam: i'll run the repro harness once alex's branch is up. If we see reinsert_rate > 0.1 and page faults spike, we can gate a rollback.
nisha: okay action items: alex -> prototype deferred requeue + metric (PR by EOD); sam -> run repro and collect flamegraphs; kevin -> audit FIFO shim for other reinsertion sites; maria -> suggest kernel_select threshold changes and a short-term rollout plan.
kevin: small note — make sure eviction_batch isn't too small; increasing batch size to 128 amortizes unlink cost and reduces churn in the eviction loop.
maria: agree. also add a canary with throttling of long-context sessions as an emergency toggle.
alex: got it. creating PR 1852 with flag `defer_requeue=true` and metric `kv.reinsert_rate`. Will link when ready. :shipit:
nisha: thanks team. keep updates in this thread. :eyes:
